entrypoints.summary: The V05 finding identifies the affected endpoint path as /businessconfig/processes on localhost:2002 in the businessconfig container; its CVSS vector records network access and high privileges required.

affected_components.file: not resolved from inspected report excerpt
affected_components.role: The audit identifies this filter as insufficient because it does not match the ../ prefix.

preconditions: The audit CVSS vector specifies network access and high privileges required.
The affected businessconfig service must expose the reported /businessconfig/processes path.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A user-supplied filename/path containing ../; exact request format and payload are not preserved in the inspected excerpt.
trigger_steps.summary: Provide path material containing the ../ prefix where a filename is processed by the affected filesystem functionality.

impacts.concept: host command execution through Docker escape

mitigations.concept: safe-character filename allowlist at filesystem boundary

relation_candidates.rationale: V05's network vector requires high privileges, and the finding describes attacker control of path material passed to filesystem APIs.
The audit attributes the bypass to the unmatched ../ prefix and labels V05 as arbitrary file write and arbitrary file delete.
The V05 title reports that the arbitrary file write/delete condition leads to RCE.

relation_candidates.dst: host command execution through Docker escape
relation_candidates.rationale: The V05 finding title reports Docker escape after RCE; exact escalation steps are not retained in the inspected excerpt.

relation_candidates.dst: safe-character filename allowlist at filesystem boundary
relation_candidates.rationale: The audit recommends validating user-supplied filenames at filesystem calls with a whitelist allowing only safe filename characters.

impact.affected_asset: Filesystem contents in the businessconfig container and, through the reported Docker-escape chain, the Docker host.
impact.attacker_capability: A network-accessible authenticated user with high privileges can convert a crafted filename/path input into filesystem modification outside the intended directory and use the reported escalation chain.
impact.security_effect: Authenticated path traversal is reported to yield arbitrary file write/delete, in-container command execution, Docker escape, and host-level command execution.

causal_trace.summary: An authenticated, high-privileged user can supply a filename/path component to the affected business-configuration path-processing functionality.
The filename safety filter is bypassable because isLinuxPathSafe() does not match the ../ prefix, allowing traversal outside the intended directory structure.
The resulting filesystem operation is characterized by the audit as arbitrary file write and arbitrary file delete rather than an operation confined to the intended application directory.
The audit finding reports that these file-operation capabilities lead to command execution in the affected environment and Docker escape.

failure.operation: Filesystem operations with traversal-controlled filename material, yielding arbitrary file write and delete

primary_invariant.statement: A user-supplied filename used by the businessconfig filesystem operation must be restricted to a safe application-controlled directory and must not traverse outside it.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The audit states that isLinuxPathSafe() fails to match the ../ prefix, enabling the supplied path material to bypass filtering and navigate outside the intended directory structure.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit explicitly names V05, its endpoint/container, the ../ filter bypass, arbitrary write/delete, and the RCE/Docker-escape outcome. The report includes a proof-of-concept/reproduction section and exploit annex, but the available inspected excerpts do not preserve exact request/payload values, an observed execution transcript, or a host-execution marker. No reviewed remediation commit or regression test is available; the repository snapshot is not tied to the audited revision.

remediation.invariant_restored: Only safe filename characters are accepted before the application invokes filesystem operations, preventing ../ traversal from selecting paths outside the intended directory.
mitigation_classes: whitelist validation of user-supplied filenames at filesystem-call boundaries
